title: Cervical Spine Oncology: Perioperative Management and Complications.
abstract: STUDY DESIGN: Narrative review. OBJECTIVE: To synthesize contemporary evidence on perioperative complications in primary and metastatic cervical spine tumor surgery and to provide an evidence-informed framework for their prevention and management. SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND DATA: Cervical spine tumor surgery converges dense neurovascular and aerodigestive anatomy with a medically fragile, frequently irradiated patient population. Although cervical metastases represent only about 8-20% of spinal metastatic disease, their mismanagement carries disproportionately severe consequences, ranging from disabling pain to high-level paralysis and death. Cervical-specific risk-stratification tools are lacking, and most available evidence is extrapolated from degenerative anterior cervical cohorts. METHODS: This is a narrative review of perioperative complications in cervical spine oncology. PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar were searched for English-language articles published through May 2026, prioritizing literature from the past 5 years while including seminal earlier references where foundational, using combinations of the terms "cervical spine," "spinal metastasis," "spinal tumor," "perioperative complications," "airway," "vertebral artery," "wound," "dysphagia," "venous thromboembolism," and "hardware failure." Reference lists of included articles were hand-searched for additional sources. Studies were selected by author consensus for relevance to the complication domains discussed; formal risk-of-bias assessment and quantitative pooling were not performed, consistent with a narrative design. Because oncology-specific evidence is limited, data derived from degenerative cervical cohorts are identified as such throughout. RESULTS: Major complication domains include airway compromise (highest with multilevel corpectomy, combined approaches, and cervicothoracic constructs), vascular and neurologic injury, CSF leak, wound failure and infection in irradiated fields, hardware failure, venous thromboembolism, and dysphagia. CONCLUSIONS: Outcomes depend on preoperative risk stratification, multidisciplinary coordination, and individualized postoperative care rather than any single intraoperative maneuver. Because the evidence base remains largely Level III-IV without validated cervical oncology-specific tools, described practices should be regarded as reasonable, evidence-informed considerations rather than standards of care.

OBJECTIVE: To synthesize contemporary evidence on perioperative complications in primary and metastatic cervical spine tumor surgery and to provide an evidence-informed framework for their prevention and management. title: The emerging molecular landscape of abdominal aortic aneurysms: non-coding RNAs as diagnostic and therapeutic targets.
abstract: An abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a progressive, often asymptomatic condition whose rupture is associated with a high mortality rate. Ultrasonography and computed tomography are established diagnostic methods, while molecular biomarkers may provide additional information about disease activity. This review discusses the potential role of non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) as diagnostic and therapeutic tools in AAAs. These molecules, including microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) and circular RNAs (circRNAs), are strongly involved in the regulation of gene expression. Through binding to their target mRNAs, miRNAs primarily suppress translation or promote mRNA degradation. Some lncRNAs and circRNAs act as miRNA sponges, affecting their availability. Here, these mechanisms are discussed by pathological function, distinguishing human tissue and circulating studies from animal, cellular and computational findings. Particular attention is given to miR-21, H19, GAS5, circCdyl and miR-26b-3p, which have functional experimental evidence or human biomarker data beyond expression profiling. Abnormal expression can be detected in peripheral blood or aortic tissue, but these findings do not necessarily predict aneurysm growth or rupture. Integration of ncRNA profiling with imaging and clinical parameters may improve the assessment of AAAs. However, prospective validation and further studies of delivery and safety are needed before these molecules can be used in clinical practice.

title: Brachial artery access for endovascular procedures: how safe is it?
abstract: PURPOSE: While femoral and radial artery access are routine for endovascular procedures, brachial artery access remains an important alternative in selected cases. This study aimed to evaluate the complication rate of percutaneous brachial artery access at a tertiary centre and identify potential risk factors for access-site complications. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective review was performed of all procedures utilising percutaneous brachial artery access over a 12.5-year period. Patient demographics, sheath size, closure technique and complications were recorded. Complications were classified according to the CIRSE classification system. RESULTS: One hundred percutaneous brachial artery punctures were identified. Sheath sizes ranged from 3 to 9 Fr; the majority (57%) using 6 Fr. Most procedures (84%) were performed for aortic, mesenteric/renal, or peripheral arterial interventions. Overall, 23 complications occurred (23%), including 9 (9%) grade 3 complications requiring additional treatment. No convincing association was identified between complication rate and patient age, gender, or sheath size. Vascular closure devices were used in seven cases, five of which resulted in complications, including three grade 3 events. CONCLUSIONS: The complication rate associated with brachial artery access in this series was higher than that reported in much of the published literature. These findings suggest that brachial artery access may be less safe than commonly perceived and that vascular closure devices should be used with caution, particularly given their off-label status for this access site. Standardised procedural protocols and post-procedural care pathways may help reduce complication rates. Broader auditing and reporting across centres are encouraged to better define best practice.

This study aimed to evaluate the complication rate of percutaneous brachial artery access at a tertiary centre and identify potential risk factors for access-site complications. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective review was performed of all procedures utilising percutaneous brachial artery access over a 12.5-year period.

title: Acute management of pelvic ring injuries: identifying common treatment principles across institutional algorithms.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Pelvic ring injuries are associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, particularly in patients presenting with hemodynamic instability and major hemorrhage. Numerous institutions have developed management algorithms for the acute treatment of pelvic ring injuries; however, the common principles underlying these pathways remain unclear. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were searched on January 8, 2026, for peer-reviewed publications published from January 1, 2006, through December 31, 2025 that described algorithms, pathways, or protocols for the acute management of pelvic ring injuries. Two independent reviewers performed study selection and data extraction. Algorithm components related to mechanical stabilization, physiologic assessment, imaging, hemorrhage control, and damage control resuscitation were extracted and compared using descriptive quantitative and qualitative synthesis. RESULTS: The search identified 328 records that underwent title and abstract screening, and 63 articles were assessed for full-text eligibility. Twenty-five studies were included in the final analysis. All included algorithms (25/25, 100%) used physiology-based decision-making. Early noninvasive mechanical stabilization was specified in 23/25 algorithms (92%); pelvic binders were specified in 17/25 (68%). Angiography with potential angioembolization was included in 19/25 algorithms (76%), exploratory laparotomy in 10/25 (40%), and resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta (REBOA) in 3/25 (12%). Computed tomography was incorporated into 20/25 algorithms (80%), whereas pelvic radiography was included in 18/25 (72%). Fracture morphology was used as a treatment decision point in 4/25 algorithms (16%), and pelvic packing was described in 20/25 publications (80%). CONCLUSION: Published algorithms for the acute management of pelvic ring injuries demonstrate substantial consistency despite institutional variation. Early mechanical stabilization, physiologic assessment, damage control resuscitation, radiologic evaluation, and structured hemorrhage-control pathways were identified as the most common components of contemporary management algorithms.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Pelvic ring injuries are associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, particularly in patients presenting with hemodynamic instability and major hemorrhage. Numerous institutions have developed management algorithms for the acute treatment of pelvic ring injuries; however, the common principles underlying these pathways remain unclear. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

title: Sex differences and prevalence of prior deep vein thrombosis among patients with incidental iliac vein compression on computed tomography.
abstract: p p p 2 PurposeThe purpose of this study was to identify risk factors and evaluate clinical outcomes associated with incidental left common iliac vein compression on CT imaging.MethodsThis is a retrospective study that reviewed venous-phase abdomen and pelvis CT scans to identify patients with incidental extrinsic compression of the left common iliac vein due to an overlying right common iliac artery. A total of 726 patients were included (364 females, 362 males; mean patient age: 61.9 ± 15.9 years). Board-certified radiologists reviewed all CT scans. Significant left iliac vein compression was defined as >50% luminal narrowing.ResultsSignificant iliac vein compression was identified in 114 (15.7%) patients and was more common in females (19.5%) versus males (11.9%) (< 0.01). Patients with iliac vein compression >50% had significantly lower BMI than those without compression (24.8 ± 6.2 vs 28.7 ± 7.2 kg/m,< 0.01). Patients with incidental left iliac vein compression had a higher rate of prior left lower extremity DVT (= 0.02).ConclusionIncidental left common iliac vein compression was present in approximately 16% of patients and was more frequent among females. Compression was associated with lower BMI and more than twice the rate of ipsilateral DVT, despite no prior diagnosis of MTS. These findings suggest that incidental iliac vein compression could have more clinical significance than previously recognized.

title: Association between low-carbohydrate diet scores and macrovascular events or all-cause mortality in adults with type 1 diabetes in Japan.
abstract: AIMS/INTRODUCTION: The effects of lifestyle factors on macrovascular events or all-cause mortality remain unclear in type 1 diabetes. We examined the associations of diet, physical activity, and sleep with these outcomes among adults with type 1 diabetes living in Japan. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter prospective cohort included 352 adults with type 1 diabetes from the Juntendo-Aso Type 1 Diabetes cohort. Lifestyle factors were assessed by questionnaire. Dietary intake was evaluated using a brief-type self-administered diet history questionnaire, from which Total, Plant, and Animal low-carbohydrate diet scores were calculated. The primary composite outcome was the first occurrence of ischemic heart disease, cerebrovascular disease, peripheral artery disease, or all-cause mortality. Associations were analyzed using Cox proportional hazards models. RESULTS: Mean age was 51.4 ± 15.1 years, mean HbA1c was 7.9 ± 1.1%, and carbohydrate accounted for 49.3% of energy intake. During follow-up, 35 participants experienced the primary composite outcome. In multivariable Cox models, the Total LCDS (HR, 0.90; 95% CI: 0.82-0.98; P = 0.012), Plant LCDS (HR, 0.85; 95% CI: 0.76-0.94; P = 0.003), and Animal LCDS (HR, 0.93; 95% CI: 0.87-0.996; P = 0.037) were inversely associated with the outcome. CONCLUSIONS: Among adults with type 1 diabetes living in Japan, low-carbohydrate dietary patterns, particularly the Plant low-carbohydrate diet score, were inversely associated with macrovascular events or all-cause mortality.

title: Contemporary Analysis of the Volume-Outcome Relationship for Patients With Nontraumatic Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Nontraumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) carries a substantial mortality burden and risk of long-term morbidity. Although prior investigations have demonstrated an inverse association between SAH admission volume and in-hospital mortality, reported thresholds remain broad. Importantly, the relative importance of both admission and procedural volume has yet to be evaluated on a national scale. We examined the association of volume metrics with outcomes in an SAH cohort. METHODS: All adult (≥18 years) hospitalizations with a primary diagnosis of nontraumatic SAH were identified from the 2016 to 2022 Nationwide Readmissions Database. Multivariable regression models were developed to evaluate the independent and joint associations of SAH admission and clipping and coiling procedural volume with in-hospital outcomes. RESULTS: P P Of an estimated 142 271 hospitalizations, index mortality was 20.2%. Following risk adjustment, both increasing SAH admission volume and clipping and coiling procedural volume were independently associated with reduced mortality. When modeled jointly, however, clipping and coiling procedural volume remained an independent predictor of mortality (adjusted odds ratio, 0.981 per 10 procedures,<0.001) whereas SAH admission volume was no longer significant (=0.40). CONCLUSIONS: Joint examination of SAH and clipping and coiling procedural volume revealed procedural caseload to be the dominant predictor of in-hospital mortality, suggesting that survival benefits historically attributed to admission volume may be more precisely explained by procedural expertise. These findings support reexamination of volume-based benchmarks in contemporary cerebrovascular care frameworks.

title: Exercise and Thoracic Aortic Aneurysms: A Paradigm Shift Toward Informed, Personalized Activity Guidelines.
abstract: Exercise is widely recognized for its cardiovascular benefits; however, its safety and role in patients with thoracic aortic aneurysms (TAAs) remains complex due to its distinctive biomechanical vulnerabilities. Fundamentally different from abdominal aortic aneurysms, TAAs develop from distinct pathophysiological processes that affect their hemodynamic responses to stressors and influence their risk of adverse aortic events. Exercise induces acute hemodynamic changes, including increased stroke volume, systolic and pulse pressures, and transient aortic stiffening. These changes impose mechanical stress on the aortic wall, potentially accelerating aneurysm progression or triggering adverse aortic events. Although moderate aerobic exercise generally appears safe with potential cardiovascular benefits, evidence supporting safe practices in TAAs is limited. Current guidelines frequently extrapolate from abdominal aortic aneurysm data, which overlook the specificities of the thoracic aorta. This review underscores the urgent need for comprehensive research, using advanced imaging, biomarker profiling, and real-time hemodynamic monitoring to understand how different exercise modalities and intensities affect TAAs. Well-designed prospective studies are crucial to improve risk stratification, optimize antihypertensive strategies, develop personalized exercise prescriptions, and provide evidence-informed guidance to patients. Perioperative strategies like prehabilitation and structured postoperative rehabilitation show promise but lack rigorous evaluation. Ultimately, this work advocates a paradigm shift from conservative inactivity toward informed, individualized physical activity regimens tailored to each patient's risk profile. This approach aims to maximize cardiovascular benefits while minimizing adverse aortic events, thereby improving overall health and quality of life in patients with TAAs.

title: Paradoxical Association of Body Mass Index With Occurrence and Mortality of Venous Thromboembolism in Hospitalized Patients: A National Hospital-Based Cohort Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The association between body mass index (BMI) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurrence and mortality is controversial. This study aimed to investigate the association of BMI with VTE occurrence and mortality and explore the consistency across age, sex, and medical specialty. METHODS: 2 2 2 2 This study included 3 199 526 inpatients at potential risk for VTE from a nationwide hospital-based cohort. Participants were categorized as lean weight (BMI <18.5 kg/m), normal weight (18.5 ≤BMI<24.0 kg/m), overweight (24.0 ≤BMI <28.0 kg/m), and obesity (BMI ≥28.0 kg/m). Odds ratios (ORs) were calculated by logistic regression models. RESULTS: P P for interaction for interaction In all participants, 59 002 (1.8%) developed VTE during hospitalization. After adjusting for the confounding factors, compared with normal weight, the risk of VTE occurrence reduced by 18% (odds ratio [OR], 0.82 [95% CI, 0.80-0.83]) in participants with overweight and 22% (OR, 0.78,[95% CI, 0.75-0.81]) in participants with obesity. The protective association of overweight/obesity was more pronounced in age ≥65 years, female patients, and surgery participants (<0.05), whereas in internal medical participants, obesity was associated with a higher risk of VTE occurrence (OR, 1.11 [95% CI, 1.01-1.21]). A total of 636 (1.1%) patients with VTE died before discharge. No significant association was observed between overweight/obesity and post-VTE mortality. However, in the surgical subgroup, obesity was associated with a lower risk of post-VTE mortality (OR, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.17-0.80],<0.05). CONCLUSION: An inverse association between BMI and VTE occurrence was observed among at-risk inpatients, most pronounced in older, female, and surgical subgroups. Notably, obesity remained a risk factor in medical patients, whereas among surgical patients who developed VTE, it was paradoxically associated with lower mortality.

title: Prophylactic Negative Pressure Wound Therapy Versus Standard Wound Care Among Lower Extremity Amputations: A Meta-Analysis.
abstract: P P Prophylactic closed incisional negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) has emerged as a promising strategy to reduce postoperative wound complications following lower extremity amputation in patients with peripheral arterial disease (PAD). We conducted a meta-analysis to evaluate whether closed incisional NPWT reduces wound complications compared with standard wound care (SWC) in this high-risk vasculopathic population. A systematic search was performed to identify studies comparing closed incisional NPWT and SWC among patients with PAD undergoing lower extremity amputation. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and CINAHL were searched from inception to January 2025 using predefined search strings. Six studies met eligibility criteria and were included in the analysis. Odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models as the primary analysis to account for anticipated clinical and methodological heterogeneity across studies. Leave-one-out analyses and an analysis excluding the study in which NPWT was delivered as part of a multifaceted care bundle were performed to assess robustness. A total of 893 patients were included, including 408 in the closed incisional NPWT group and 485 in the SWC group. Closed incisional NPWT was associated with lower odds of postoperative surgical site infection (SSI) (OR = 0.370; 95% CI = 0.143-0.957; = .044) and wound dehiscence (OR = 0.224; 95% CI = 0.125-0.401; = .008). Closed incisional NPWT was associated with lower odds of postoperative SSI and wound dehiscence following lower extremity amputation in patients with PAD. Because the evidence is predominantly observational and prediction intervals included the null value, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed in adequately powered randomized trials.

A systematic search was performed to identify studies comparing closed incisional NPWT and SWC among patients with PAD undergoing lower extremity amputation.

title: Approach to the patient with elevated lipoprotein(a).
abstract: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a common, genetically determined lipoprotein that is independently associated with myocardial infarction, stroke, peripheral artery disease, and calcific aortic stenosis. Because Lp(a) levels are stable over time and minimally influenced by lifestyle, the 2026 ACC/AHA/Multisociety Dyslipidemia Guideline now recommends one-time measurement in all adults and cascade screening in high-risk families; as a result, endocrinologists can expect to encounter and manage elevated Lp(a) frequently in routine clinical practice. Despite its clinical importance, no approved drug therapies specifically targeting Lp(a) yet exist; therefore, management should currently focus on aggressive optimization of traditional risk factors, particularly LDL-C lowering with statins and selective use of adjunctive therapies such as PCSK9 inhibitors and lipid apheresis. Emerging evidence suggests a potential benefit of selective aspirin use, while novel therapeutics-antisense oligonucleotides and small interfering RNAs-which robustly lower Lp(a) are currently being tested in phase 3 clinical trials. We present case-based examples to highlight practical approaches to risk assessment and management of elevated Lp(a).

title: Blunt Thoracic Aortic Injury in the Geriatric Population: Results from the Aortic Trauma Foundation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The management of blunt thoracic aortic injury (BTAI) is evolving as the trauma population ages, yet the impact of age on treatment patterns and outcomes remains incompletely defined. STUDY DESIGN: A retrospective analysis of the Aortic Trauma Foundation registry (November 2016 to November 2023) identified 823 patients with BTAI, including 118 geriatric patients (65 years and older). Demographics, injury characteristics, management strategies, and outcomes were compared between the geriatric and younger (younger than 65 years) cohorts. RESULTS: Geriatric patients more frequently presented after falls (17.8% vs 6.7%, p < 0.0001) and had a higher proportion of grade IV injuries (18.5% vs 9.2%, p = 0.0021), with no difference in admission systolic blood pressure (116 vs 116, p = 0.960) or Injury Severity Score (31 vs 33, p = 0.150). Management strategies were similar between groups, including nonoperative (37.3% vs 36.9%, p = 0.932), open (4.2% vs 1.9%, p = 0.132), and endovascular repair (58.5% vs 61.1%, p = 0.584). Despite comparable treatment approaches, geriatric patients had higher in-hospital mortality (27.1% vs 10.9%, p < 0.0001) and aortic-related mortality (8.5% vs 3.4%, p = 0.010). CONCLUSIONS: Geriatric patients with BTAI sustain more severe injuries and experience significantly higher mortality despite similar management strategies. These findings suggest that current treatment paradigms may not adequately address age-associated risk and highlight the need for age-specific management considerations.

title: Targeting Nupr1-Mediated p53 Mitochondrial Sequestration Alleviates Aortic Dissection by Restoring the Gadd45b-Dependent Survival Program.
abstract: Aortic dissection (AD) is a catastrophic cardiovascular emergency triggered by severe pathological stress. While continuous stress drives vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) apoptosis via mitochondrial dysfunction, the precise upstream orchestrators linking these stress signals to the mitochondrial apoptotic cascade remain elusive. By integrating clinical observations and single-cell RNA sequencing, we found that Nuclear Protein 1 (Nupr1), a critical stress-responsive factor, is significantly upregulated in aortas from AD patients and murine models, with enrichment in VSMCs. Remarkably, VSMC-specific Nupr1 deficiency significantly ameliorated AD progression in vivo. Mechanistically, Nupr1 undergoes massive mitochondrial accumulation in Ang II-induced apoptotic VSMCs. Rather than operating as a conventional transcriptional regulator, mitochondrially enriched Nupr1 functions as a pathological spatial switch. It sequesters p53 within mitochondria, driving transcription-independent apoptosis while simultaneously blunting the protective Gadd45b-mediated survival program. Furthermore, in vivo Gadd45b overexpression was sufficient to rescue mitochondrial dysfunction and ameliorate vascular collapse. Taken together, our findings conceptualize the Nupr1-p53-Gadd45b axis as an important determinant of VSMC fate and provide a novel and promising therapeutic strategy for preventing AD progression.

title: Successful First-Line Haploidentical Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation in an Elderly Patient With Severe Aplastic Anemia and Complex Comorbidities: A Case Report.
abstract: Standard management guidelines generally recommend immunosuppressive therapy (IST) as first-line treatment for older patients with severe aplastic anemia (SAA), whereas the role of upfront haploidentical hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (haplo-HSCT) in this population remains uncertain, particularly in patients with complex comorbidities. We report a 62-year-old woman with SAA, a history of surgically resected stage IA lung adenocarcinoma, and previous left lower extremity deep vein thrombosis treated with venous stent implantation and long-term aspirin therapy. Because no matched sibling or unrelated donor was available, and following individualized counseling regarding IST and transplantation, the patient underwent upfront haplo-HSCT combined with umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells after a conditioning regimen including fludarabine, busulfan, cyclophosphamide, antithymocyte globulin, and thiotepa. Neutrophil engraftment occurred on post-transplant day +12, and platelet independence was achieved on day +13. Donor chimerism reached 99.6% by day +14 and remained within the complete-chimerism range through the latest available assessment in January 2026. In late December 2025 and January 2026, the patient developed cytomegalovirus infection accompanied by transient trilineage cytopenia; after anti-CMV treatment with maribavir, the infection was controlled and peripheral blood counts subsequently recovered. At the most recent clinical follow-up on August 6, 2026, approximately 17 months after transplantation, no chronic graft-versus-host disease had developed, the previous lung adenocarcinoma remained in remission, and the thrombotic condition remained clinically stable. This case suggests that upfront haplo-HSCT combined with UC-MSCs may represent a feasible individualized treatment option for carefully selected older patients with SAA who lack matched donors, although broader conclusions require larger studies and longer follow-up.

We report a 62-year-old woman with SAA, a history of surgically resected stage IA lung adenocarcinoma, and previous left lower extremity deep vein thrombosis treated with venous stent implantation and long-term aspirin therapy. Because no matched sibling or unrelated donor was available, and following individualized counseling regarding IST and transplantation, the patient underwent upfront haplo-HSCT combined with umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells after a conditioning regimen including fludarabine, busulfan, cyclophosphamide, antithymocyte globulin, and thiotepa.

title: Optimizing pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis in medical inpatients using sequential IMPROVE risk assessment models: Clinical, economic and environmental implications.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major preventable cause of morbidity and mortality in hospitalized medical patients. Current recommendations support broad pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis, while individualized risk assessment may help refine prescribing. The IMPROVE VTE and IMPROVE Bleeding scores provide standardized risk assessment tools but should complement, rather than replace, clinical judgment. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the discrepancy between real-world thromboprophylaxis prescribing and a prespecified sequential IMPROVE-based strategy and assess its economic and environmental implications. METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study in internal medicine over one month. Adults hospitalized for>48h were included, excluding those receiving therapeutic anticoagulation. IMPROVE VTE and Bleeding scores were calculated retrospectively. Pharmacologic prophylaxis was supported by the strategy for patients with an IMPROVE Bleeding score<7 and IMPROVE VTE score≥2. Observed prescriptions were compared with the prespecified strategy using contingency analysis and Fisher's exact test. RESULTS: 2 Among 99 patients, 79.8% received pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis, whereas 46.5% met the strategy criteria. Among treated patients, 46.8% did not meet these criteria. Strict application of the strategy would theoretically result in 292 fewer doses over one month, corresponding to €233.60 in estimated savings and approximately 405kg COeq. CONCLUSION: Real-world prescribing differed substantially from the prespecified strategy. Strict application would theoretically reduce anticoagulant use, costs, and carbon emissions. However, clinical outcomes were not assessed, and RAMs should complement rather than replace clinical judgment. Prospective studies incorporating VTE and bleeding outcomes are required to assess the safety of this approach.

title: Microsurgical Clipping of a Tumor-Like Bilobulated Ophthalmic Aneurysm: A 2-Dimensional Operative Video.
abstract: 1-3 4-6 2,4,7 ,8 Ophthalmic artery aneurysm are technically challenging lesions because of their complex paraclinoid anatomy and intimate relationship with the optic apparatus, internal carotid artery (ICA), and ophthalmic artery.Visual dysfunction is an important clinical presentation, particularly in large aneurysms causing optic nerve compression, and visual outcomes remain a major consideration when selecting among microsurgical and endovascular treatment strategies.Microsurgical clipping remains an important option in selected complex aneurysms because it provides definitive exclusion while allowing direct optic nerve decompression and parent-vessel reconstruction.. We present the operative video of 59-year-old woman with progressive right-predominant visual deterioration over approximately 30 days. Imaging demonstrated a large, irregular, bilobulated ophthalmic artery aneurysm measuring 18 x 11 mm, with an 8 mm neck and postcontrast wall enhancement. Given the progressive visual deficit and optic nerve compression, microsurgical treatment was selected. Following proximal cervical ICA control and a pterional-transsylvian approachthe optic nerve was decompressed and the aneurysm exposed. Its broad neck and complex bilobulated morphology required tandem clip reconstruction of the ICA while preserving ophthalmic artery flow. Motor-evoked potentials and indocyanine green videoangiography guided clip adjustment. Atherosclerotic plaque at ophthalmic artery origin further influenced final clip positioning. Postoperative CTA confirmed parent-vessel patency, and visual field testing demonstrated improvement at 2 weeks. This video demonstrates optic nerve decompression, reconstructive clipping, and flow-preserving microsurgical strategies for a complex ophthalmic artery aneurysm.

title: Long-Term Durability of Bare-Metal Stenting in Complex Iliac Disease: External Iliac Artery Involvement as the Principal Determinant of Late Patency Loss.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Long-term durability after endovascular treatment of complex aortoiliac disease remains incompletely defined. The present study evaluated late primary patency after bare-metal stenting (BMS) in TASC C-D lesions and examined whether anatomical extension beyond the common iliac artery influences long-term outcomes independently of traditional TASC classification. METHODS: A single-center retrospective cohort study was conducted including 153 consecutive iliac limbs with TASC C-D occlusive disease treated with BMS between 2014 and 2024. Covered stents, kissing configurations, and acute occlusions were excluded to ensure a homogeneous technical cohort. The primary endpoint was primary patency. Kaplan-Meier estimates were reported through 72 months. Restricted mean survival time (RMST) regression at τ = 72 months and Firth penalized logistic regression were applied to identify independent predictors while minimizing small-event bias. RESULTS: Technical success exceeded 97%, with no perioperative mortality. Primary patency remained high and comparable between TASC C and D lesions at 72 months (86% vs 84%; log-rank p = 0.8). In contrast, extension into the external iliac artery (EIA) was associated with progressive late attrition. Adjusted RMST analysis demonstrated a 7.6-month reduction in mean primary patency at 72 months for EIA-involved lesions (95% CI -11.6 to -3.6; p < 0.001). Firth regression confirmed increased late risk of patency loss at 60 months (OR 10.5; p = 0.034) and 72 months (OR 25.8; p = 0.003). Technical optimization (best-practice stenting) showed limited and model-dependent mitigation, without consistent protection across time points. CONCLUSIONS: In complex iliac BMS reconstruction, long-term durability appears primarily determined by distal anatomical extension rather than TASC class. External iliac artery involvement identifies a subgroup at risk for late failure and may represent a more clinically meaningful stratification parameter for endovascular planning.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Long-term durability after endovascular treatment of complex aortoiliac disease remains incompletely defined. The present study evaluated late primary patency after bare-metal stenting (BMS) in TASC C-D lesions and examined whether anatomical extension beyond the common iliac artery influences long-term outcomes independently of traditional TASC classification. METHODS: A single-center retrospective cohort study was conducted including 153 consecutive iliac limbs with TASC C-D occlusive disease treated with BMS between 2014 and 2024.

title: Contemporary Management of Subclavian and Axillary Artery Aneurysms in Connective Tissue Disease: Navigating Therapeutic Uncertainty in a Rare Vascular Disease Without Dedicated Guidelines.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Subclavian artery aneurysms (SAAs) represent one of the rarest forms of peripheral arterial aneurysmal disease. Despite their low incidence, management in patients with underlying connective tissue disorders poses specific challenges related to intrinsic vessel fragility. Because of their rarity, the available literature is largely confined to case reports and small, heterogeneous retrospective series, and management remains largely experience-based rather than evidence-based. Explicit guidance from the Society for Vascular Surgery and the European Society for Vascular Surgery is lacking. METHODS: We performed a systematic review of the English-language literature to identify all reported cases of subclavian and axillary artery aneurysms in patients with heritable connective-tissue disorders. Searches were conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception to June 30, 2025. Data were extracted on treatment modality (open surgical, endovascular, or hybrid) and clinical outcomes (limb loss, revascularization patency, complications, and need for reintervention). The review protocol was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420261332695) RESULTS: Of 142 records identified, 24 studies met the inclusion criteria after duplicate removal and screening. These studies described 43 subclavian and axillary artery aneurysms in 25 patients (15 men [60%] and 10 women [40%]; median age, 46 years; range, 11-68). Aneurysm diameter was reported for 36 of 43 aneurysms (84%; median, 40 mm; range, 22-100 mm) and was not reported for the remaining 7 (16%). Marfan syndrome was the most frequent underlying disorder (20/25, 80%), followed by vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome type IV (3/25, 12%) and Loeys-Dietz syndrome/TGFBR2-related arteriopathy (2/25, 8%). Eight aneurysms (8/43, 19%) required urgent or emergent treatment. Treatment modalities comprised open surgical repair in 22 of 43 aneurysms (51%) - including interposition grafting in 12/22 (55%), bypass in 5/22 (23%), arterial ligation in 3/22 (14%), and aneurysmectomy with end-to-end anastomosis in 2/22 (9%) - hybrid procedures in 15 (35%), and endovascular therapy in 6 (14%) - including covered stent-grafting in 5/6 (83%) and coil/liquid embolization in 1/6 (17%). Immediate technical success - complete aneurysm exclusion without endoleak at the index procedure- was 95% (41 of 43 aneurysms). Two aneurysms (4.7%), both in the hybrid group, represented an index-procedure failure due to endoleak (one type I, one type III); freedom from reintervention was therefore 95% (41/43). Both were subsequently excluded after a secondary reintervention, yielding a delayed technical success rate of 100% (43/43). No 30-day mortality or limb loss was reported. Primary patency of the treated segment was 100% (43/43), as no graft/segment thrombosis, occlusion, or flow-limiting stenosis occurred; secondary patency was 100% (43/43). Where a numeric follow-up duration could be extracted, mean follow-up was 8 months (range, 6-11 months) in the endovascular group (4/5 patients), 15 months (range, 2 weeks-4 years) in the open group (5/13 patients), and 15 months (range, 1-60 months) in the hybrid group (6/7 patients); a precise duration was not reported for the remaining patients. CONCLUSION: The available evidence demonstrates that both open and endovascular repair can achieve satisfactory short- and mid-term outcomes. However, patient selection, procedural planning, and surveillance protocols remain poorly standardized. The observed recurrences and the limited duration of follow-up reported in the literature underscore the need for rigorous, lifelong surveillance. Prospective multicenter registries are warranted to refine best practice and to guide the development of devices and techniques tailored to fragile connective-tissue vessels.

Despite their low incidence, management in patients with underlying connective tissue disorders poses specific challenges related to intrinsic vessel fragility. Because of their rarity, the available literature is largely confined to case reports and small, heterogeneous retrospective series, and management remains largely experience-based rather than evidence-based.

title: In-hospital vascular surgery consultation is associated with improved follow-up and earlier identification of aneurysmal degeneration after acute Type A aortic dissection.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Acute Type A aortic dissections (TAAD) are historically managed by cardiac surgery. However, subsequent treatment of residual dissection within the thoracoabdominal aorta often requires vascular surgical intervention and lifelong surveillance. This study assesses long-term outcomes by completeness of follow-up after operative intervention for acute TAAD. METHODS: Patients who underwent surgical intervention for acute TAAD from 2014 to 2025 were identified. Patients who experienced death within 30-days or those with dissection limited to Zone 0/Zone 1 were excluded. Vascular surgery evaluation and time to consultation (index-hospitalization, outpatient, none) was documented. Follow-up was classified as complete, incomplete, or lost (LTF) according to the frequency of contrasted thoracoabdominal imaging, consistent with clinical practice guidelines. Trends in completeness of follow-up were described. Demographics, anatomic/operative characteristics, and perioperative outcomes were compared between complete follow-up and incomplete follow-up/LTF groups. Long-term outcomes (aortic degeneration, planned secondary intervention, survival) were assessed with Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox regression analysis. RESULTS: 241 patients were included; 80% had vascular surgery consultation (70% inpatient, 30% outpatient) and 86% of consultations occurred within 1-year of index procedure. In total, 46% of patients had complete follow-up, 41% had incomplete follow-up, and 13% were LTF. In-hospital consultation increased by 58% over the study period. Demographics, comorbidities, and anatomic characteristics were similar between groups. Patients with complete follow-up had higher rates of complex arch repair (Zone 1-3) (complete 56% vs. incomplete/LTF 27%, p<0.001), were more likely to undergo genetic testing (complete 52% vs. incomplete/LTF 18%, p<0.001), in-hospital TEVAR extension (7% vs. 2%, p=0.028), and TEVAR extension within 3 months (complete 17% vs. incomplete/LTF 5%, p=0.002). In time-to-event analysis, complete follow-up was associated with more planned secondary interventions (complete: 12% vs. incomplete: 5%, p=0.007) and identified aneurysmal degeneration (32% vs. 15%, p=0.002) within 1-year of acute dissection. Long-term survival differed by completeness of follow-up; 1-year (complete: 97% vs. incomplete: 97% vs. LTF: 91%), 3-years (complete: 92% vs. incomplete: 95% vs. LTF: 81%, p=0.021). There were no aortic-related deaths for patients with complete follow-up and five aortic-related deaths (5%) in patients with incomplete follow-up (p=0.13). In-hospital vascular surgery consultation was associated with complete follow-up (HR 2.87, 95% CI 1.6-5.1) and planned secondary interventions (HR 2.07, 95% CI 1.1-3.9). CONCLUSION: Vascular surgery consultation is associated with increased identification of aneurysmal degeneration, planned secondary interventions, and mid-term survival. These data suggest that longitudinal vascular surgical care, starting with in-hospital consultation, is a critical component of care following acute TAAD and should be strongly considered to ensure appropriate postoperative surveillance and improve long-term patient outcomes.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Acute Type A aortic dissections (TAAD) are historically managed by cardiac surgery. However, subsequent treatment of residual dissection within the thoracoabdominal aorta often requires vascular surgical intervention and lifelong surveillance. This study assesses long-term outcomes by completeness of follow-up after operative intervention for acute TAAD.

title: Reintervention Burden and Patency of Hemodialysis Vascular Access in a 15-Year Single-Center Cohort.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Maintaining a hemodialysis access typically requires repeated intervention, yet the cumulative reintervention burden-as distinct from patency-is rarely quantified, and configuration-specific estimates from Asian centers are scarce. We evaluated patency and quantified the configuration-specific reintervention burden of upper-extremity arteriovenous accesses over 15 years at a single center. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 871 consecutive upper-extremity arteriovenous accesses (648 fistulas; 223 grafts) created in 810 patients between 2009 and 2024. Every subsequent procedure was adjudicated from operative records as patency-maintaining or access-abandoning; operations unrelated to the access under study, including kidney transplantation, catheter procedures, and peripheral arterial interventions, were excluded. Patency was estimated by the Kaplan-Meier method according to accepted reporting standards and compared across configurations-radiocephalic fistula, brachiocephalic fistula, basilic vein transposition, and graft. The reintervention burden was expressed as interventions per access-year. Predictors of loss of primary patency were assessed by multivariable Cox regression, and a competing-risk analysis treated kidney transplantation as a competing event. RESULTS: Median follow-up was 14.7 months. Overall primary, assisted-primary, and secondary patency were 60.3%, 50.5%, and 44.6%; 87.1%, 81.5%, and 77.1%; and 96.8%, 95.7%, and 94.1% at 1, 2, and 3 years, respectively. One-year primary patency differed by configuration: 70.1% for radiocephalic fistulas, 63.3% for brachiocephalic fistulas, 71.6% for basilic vein transpositions, and 36.2% for grafts (P < .001). Across 2211 access-years, 743 patency-maintaining interventions were performed (0.336 per access-year), and 37.2% of accesses required at least one reintervention. The burden was concentrated in grafts: 1.09 interventions per access-year for grafts versus 0.25 for autogenous fistulas, an approximately 4.4-fold difference. Graft configuration (hazard ratio, 2.39; 95% confidence interval, 1.86-3.06), female sex (1.37; 1.10-1.71), ischemic heart disease (1.42; 1.04-1.94), and diabetes (1.26; 1.00-1.57) independently predicted loss of primary patency. Findings persisted after excluding maturation-assisting procedures and in the competing-risk analysis (graft subdistribution hazard ratio for reintervention, 2.32). CONCLUSIONS: High secondary patency was achieved at the cost of substantial reintervention concentrated in grafts, which required roughly 4.4 times the maintenance of autogenous fistulas. Reporting an explicit reintervention burden alongside patency supports autogenous-first, configuration-aware access planning and patient counseling.

We evaluated patency and quantified the configuration-specific reintervention burden of upper-extremity arteriovenous accesses over 15 years at a single center. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 871 consecutive upper-extremity arteriovenous accesses (648 fistulas; 223 grafts) created in 810 patients between 2009 and 2024.

title: Limb Salvage is Possible in Select Patients with Arterial Injuries and Elevated Mangled Extremity Severity Scores.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Lower extremity trauma with vascular compromise is frequently associated with other injuries and requires emergent and complex decision-making. The Mangled Extremity Severity Score (MESS) is widely utilized to predict the need for amputation in these cases. As the tool was developed over 30 years ago, its accuracy in a modern trauma setting remains a topic of investigation and discussion. The purpose of this study was to investigate the correlation of an elevated MESS with the need for amputation in patients with traumatic lower extremity arterial injuries. METHODS: A retrospective chart review was performed on patients ≥18 years old with traumatic lower extremity arterial injuries at a level I trauma center from July 2012 to December 2023. Demographics, injury characteristics, interventions, and outcomes including amputation upon presentation, amputation during hospitalization, and amputation after discharge following limb salvage attempts were recorded. RESULTS: In our cohort of 238 limbs with lower extremity arterial injury, median age was 33 years and majority of the patients were male (84.1%). The predominant mechanism was penetrating (65.1%). Eighty-four lower extremity injures had concomitant injuries (35.3%). The median MESS was 5 (IQR 3-6). Vascular repair was performed on 179 lower limbs (75.2%); 168 were open repairs (93.9%), nine endovascular (5.0%), and two hybrid (1.1%). Ninety-two limbs underwent concomitant orthopedic repair (38.7%). Six limbs underwent primary amputation (2.5%) after multidisciplinary consensus, all of which had a MESS ≥7. Of the 179 lower limbs that underwent vascular repair, 8.4% required amputation prior to discharge, and another 2.8% after discharge. Thirty-three lower extremities with a MESS ≥7 underwent vascular repair. The majority did not require a subsequent amputation (22/33, 66.7%). In the entire cohort, a MESS ≥ 7 was found to be significantly associated with any amputation (P<.0001) when compared to MESS <7. MESS ≥7 had significantly greater odds of amputation in both univariable (OR = 10.6; 95% CI: 4.65-24.1; p<0.0001) and multivariable analysis after adjusting for age, ischemia time, mechanism of injury, concomitant injuries, arterial injury location, and fracture status (aOR = 5.40; 95% CI: 1.79-16.3; p=0.003). CONCLUSION: Lower extremity arterial injuries are frequently associated with complex orthopedic and soft tissue trauma. An increasing MESS, blunt mechanism, and the presence of multiple vascular injuries are significantly associated with the risk of limb loss. While a MESS of 7 or greater is predictive of an increased risk of amputation, limb salvage can still be achieved in many patients with prompt vascular repair despite high MESS.

The Mangled Extremity Severity Score (MESS) is widely utilized to predict the need for amputation in these cases. As the tool was developed over 30 years ago, its accuracy in a modern trauma setting remains a topic of investigation and discussion.

title: Efficacy and Safety of No Thromboprophylaxis after Endovenous Radiofrequency Ablation for Incompetent Saphenous VeiNs: the TRAIN Non-inferiority Randomised Controlled Trial.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The benefit of post-operative pharmacological thromboprophylaxis after endovenous radiofrequency ablation (RFA) for incompetent saphenous veins in patients without previous deep vein thrombosis (DVT) of the lower limbs is unclear. This trial compared no extended thromboprophylaxis with extended anticoagulation after RFA. METHODS: TRAIN (Thromboprophylaxis after endovenous Radiofrequency Ablation for Incompetent saphenous veiNs) was a multicentre, evaluator blinded, non-inferiority randomised controlled trial. Adults with primary great saphenous vein incompetence undergoing RFA, with concomitant tributary phlebectomy and or ultrasound guided foam sclerotherapy when clinically indicated, were enrolled. Patients with previous DVT of the lower limbs were excluded. All participants received a single intra-operative intravenous dose of unfractionated heparin and were randomised to either no extended pharmacological thromboprophylaxis or rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily for fourteen days post-operatively. The primary outcome was thrombosis related events within thirty days. RESULTS: Of 406 patients screened, 354 were included in the intention to treat analysis and 304 in the per protocol analysis. The no extended thromboprophylaxis strategy was non-inferior to fourteen days of rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily for thrombosis related events (risk difference -1.34%, 95% confidence interval -7.53 - 4.84%; p = .022 for non-inferiority). One participant in the anticoagulation group (one of 177; 0.6%) experienced clinically relevant non-major bleeding on post-operative day 10. No bleeding event occurred in the no anticoagulation group (0 of 177; p = 1.0). CONCLUSION: Omitting extended post-operative rivaroxaban thromboprophylaxis after RFA with concomitant phlebectomy and sclerotherapy in patients without previous DVT was non-inferior to fourteen days of rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily for thrombosis related events. Prophylactic rivaroxaban was not associated with an increased risk of bleeding.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: The benefit of post-operative pharmacological thromboprophylaxis after endovenous radiofrequency ablation (RFA) for incompetent saphenous veins in patients without previous deep vein thrombosis (DVT) of the lower limbs is unclear. This trial compared no extended thromboprophylaxis with extended anticoagulation after RFA. title: Optimizing Vessel Preparation in Femoropopliteal Lesions: Does the Chocolate Balloon Deliver on Its Clinical Promise?
abstract: The "leave nothing behind" paradigm using drug-coated balloons (DCBs) has reshaped femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease treatment, though clinical success remains heavily contingent upon optimal vessel preparation. In a recent issue of The American Journal of Cardiology, Li and colleagues address the limitations of conventional plain old balloon angioplasty (POBA) through a propensity score-matched analysis of 508 patients from the multicenter PROMISING registry, comparing specialized vessel preparation using the nitinol-constrained Chocolate balloon against POBA prior to DCB angioplasty. The Chocolate balloon significantly reduced the primary endpoint of bailout stenting (20.47% vs. 29.92%) and facilitated larger final DCB diameters, though these acute mechanical advantages did not translate into statistically significant differences in clinical outcomes at 12 months. This commentary examines this striking "procedural-to-clinical paradox," highlighting how the potent antiproliferative effect of DCBs and the acute compensatory function of bailout stents may temporarily mask early clinical divergence. Given that cumulative mechanical failures of permanent metallic implants typically emerge beyond one year in hostile biomechanical environments, longer-term observation remains essential to capture the true clinical dividend of a stent-free strategy.

title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Use Before Total Knee Arthroplasty is Associated With Lower Postoperative MI, DVT, and VTE Rates.
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RA) are increasingly prescribed for glycemic control and weight management, but their association with postoperative thrombotic events after total knee arthroplasty remains unclear. We performed a retrospective cohort study using deidentified data from the TriNetX United States Collaborative Network, including adults who underwent primary total knee arthroplasty between December 1, 2006 and June 1, 2025. Patients with prior myocardial infarction, deep vein thrombosis, venous thromboembolism, or pulmonary embolism were excluded. Exposure was defined as a prescription for a GLP-1 RA within 1 year and 1 day before surgery. A 1:1 propensity score match was performed on demographics, relevant comorbidities, and medications, yielding 11,765 patients in each cohort. Outcomes were postoperative myocardial infarction, deep vein thrombosis, venous thromboembolism, and pulmonary embolism. Compared with matched controls, patients prescribed GLP-1 receptor agonists had a significantly lower risk of myocardial infarction (25/11,246 vs 47/11,171; risk ratio [RR] 0.528; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.325 - 0.858). GLP-1 RA use was also associated with a reduced risk of deep vein thrombosis (74/11,319 vs 103/11,308; RR 0.718; 95% CI, 0.533 - 0.966) and venous thromboembolism (133/11,040 vs 172/11,027; RR 0.772; 95% CI, 0.617 - 0.967). In contrast, no statistically significant difference was observed in the incidence of pulmonary embolism between groups (49/11,352 vs 58/11,382; RR 0.847; 95% CI, 0.580 - 1.238). Overall, preoperative GLP-1 receptor agonist use was associated with a significantly lower postoperative risk of myocardial infarction, deep vein thrombosis, and venous thromboembolism following total knee arthroplasty in this large, nationally representative cohort.

title: The Moderating Effects of Race and Ethnicity on a Motivational Interviewing Intervention for Improving Physical Health Among Patients With Peripheral Artery Disease: Secondary Analysis of a Pilot Randomized Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In a pilot randomized trial, face-to-face or telephone motivational interviewing (MI) was more efficacious than a smartphone app after 3 months for increasing 6-minute walk distance (primary outcome) and reducing body weight (secondary outcome) in patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD). Little is known about intervention heterogeneity related to social determinants of health (SDOH). OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore whether SDOH are associated with the MI intervention effects on walking distance and weight loss and generate intervention heterogeneity hypotheses. METHODS: Community dwellers in Wichita, Kansas, were recruited through community outlets and screened for PAD. Consented participants were randomly assigned to MI (n=16) or an app (n=13). Survey instruments were used to measure SDOH, demographics, and adverse childhood experiences, which were assessed for their associations with 6-minute walk distance change and weight loss. Difference-in-differences (DiD) comparisons of median changes between SDOH strata were conducted using Wilcoxon and Kruskal-Wallis nonparametric tests. RESULTS: For 6-minute walk distance, pretest-posttest changes were significantly greater among participants of "other" race and ethnicity than among non-Hispanic White participants (DiD=44.0 m, 95% CI 19.2-164.2; P=.004), and no DiDs for other SDOH were significant. Significant median pretest-posttest increases in walking distance were observed in those with a college or higher educational attainment (48.8 m, 95% CI 28.0-61.4), unmarried individuals (40.4 m, 95% CI 0.5-56.0), those living with family (55.7 m, 95% CI 30.5-199.5), those who talked to and saw family or friends 3 or more times a week (46.4 m, 95% CI 17.2-69.4), and those without unmet daily needs (46.5 m, 95% CI 7.6-67.1). For weight loss, we did not observe significant DiDs with any SDOH. However, a significant median weight loss was observed in every SDOH stratum where we observed a significant increase in 6-minute walk distance. Significant weight loss was also observed in 5 additional SDOH strata: male individuals, household income below US $30,000, never served in military, employed status, and no stress. The improvements in weight loss and walking distance were highly consistent in both direction and size across SDOH strata. CONCLUSIONS: This pilot study was the first to explore potential SDOH-related intervention effect modification and heterogeneity. The significant association between walking distance and race and ethnicity suggested a potential effect modification. Significant pretest-posttest improvements in both outcomes were found in the same SDOH strata. The highly consistent evidence across both outcomes and all SDOH strata provided confidence in potential intervention efficacy and heterogeneity despite the small sample size. Our findings were consistent with established associations between SDOH and general functions in patients with PAD, suggesting likely mediation pathways through health literacy and social support. Future interventions should consider heterogeneity to target socially disadvantaged patients with PAD to bridge disparities and maximize benefits. title: Lived experiences of post-traumatic growth in patients with acute type A aortic dissection: A qualitative study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Acute type A aortic dissection is a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency characterized by sudden onset, severe pain, and high mortality, exerting profound physical and psychological burdens on affected individuals. While negative psychological sequelae predominate in most cases, a subset of patients demonstrates remarkable resilience, manifesting post-traumatic growth-a positive psychological transformation emerging in the aftermath of trauma. This qualitative study aimed to investigate the lived experiences of post-traumatic growth among Acute type A aortic dissection survivors, shedding light on this understudied dimension of their recovery trajectory. METHODS: A qualitative study was conducted using a phenomenological approach. Twenty patients diagnosed with Acute type A aortic dissection were recruited through purposive sampling from a tertiary hospital in China. Data were collected via in-depth, face-to-face semi-structured interviews and analyzed using Colaizzi's seven-step method to extract key themes and sub-themes. RESULTS: Three overarching themes and eight sub-themes were identified, reflecting the multidimensional nature of post-traumatic growth in Acute type A aortic dissection patients: Reevaluating Life Priorities (reordering life priorities, valuing life), Behavioral Transformation (improving unhealthy habits, enhancing treatment adherence), and Enhanced Social Connections (strengthened family ties, gratitude for social support, reintegration into family and society, altruistic behavior). CONCLUSIONS: This study elucidates three core dimensions of post-traumatic growth in survivors of acute type A aortic dissection: life priority reassessment, adoption of positive health behaviors, and enhanced social connectedness. The findings underscore the critical role of guided self-reflection, supported behavior change, and robust family-social support systems in facilitating psychological recovery. We recommend integrating interventions focused on post-traumatic growth, such as psychological counseling and structured family support, into standard cardiac rehabilitation protocols to promote holistic recovery. Together, these insights provide a theoretical and practical foundation for developing tailored psychosocial interventions for this patient population.

title: PERCUTANEOUS MECHANICAL THROMBECTOMY: A NEW TOOL IN THE TREATMENT OF ACUTE MESENTERIC ISCHEMIA.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The diagnosis of acute mesenteric ischemia (AMI) remains challenging due to nonspecific symptoms and signs that lead to a high mortality rate. Common causes include cardiac emboli and thrombosis of a mesenteric plaque. OBJECTIVE: To present a clinical case of acute mesenteric ischemia that underwent successful endovascular revascularization. CASE REPORT: 82-year-old female patient with a history of atrioventricular block, hypertension, and dementia. She was admitted to the emergency department for acute abdominal pain with onset 3 days before. Diagnosis of ischemic colitis secondary to acute superior mesenteric artery occlusion was confirmed by angioCT scan. Endovascular treatment was performed: percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy through left brachial access using the Rotarex® system (Straub Medical). She improved from her previous symptoms and was discharged at day 6, with no need of exploratory laparotomy. DISCUSSION/CONCLUSION: AMI is a vascular emergency that requires rapid identification and treatment. There are two courses of action for mesenteric revascularization: open or endovascular. Some authors have demonstrated an advantage in the endovascular approach, with reduced morbidity and mortality, especially in an often aging and frail group of patients. The Rotarex® (Straub Medical) system fragments the thrombus and aspirates it at the same time, thus avoiding embolic phenomena at distance. Despite being a new technology, it has shown to be a very promising tool for AMI treatment due to its fast restoration of blood flow with minimal invasiveness.

title: Progress on the related mechanisms of vascular calcification in autogenous arteriovenous fistula in hemodialysis patients.
abstract: Autologous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred vascular access for end-stage renal disease patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis as a replacement therapy. As the duration of dialysis increases, the risk of vascular access-related complications such as AVF stenosis, thrombosis, vascular calcification (VC), and aneurysm formation gradually rises. Among these, VC has been proven to be independently associated with the occurrence and mortality of cardiovascular diseases in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). VC in the AVF of dialysis patients can lead to AVF failure, severely limiting its usability and increasing the risk of mortality among dialysis patients. Unlike previous reviews that predominantly focused on isolated mechanisms such as mineral metabolism or arterial calcification, this narrative review innovatively integrates the crosstalk among hemodynamic stress, inflammation, oxidative stress, deficiency of endogenous calcification inhibitors and pathological matrix remodeling, thereby providing a multidimensional perspective on AVF-VC. This review reframes the current understanding of AVF-VC, shifting it from a generalized complication of CKD-mineral and bone disorder to a distinct, fistula-specific pathological entity. This conceptual advancement offers a theoretical foundation for developing precision intervention strategies tailored to the unique microenvironment of the AVF.

title: Circulatory arrest versus aortic cross-clamping in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm repair.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Aortic cross‑clamping and mild hypothermic circulatory arrest (MHCA) are commonly used strategies in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm surgery. This study compared these approaches in elective procedures for patients with a distal ascending aortic diameter of 40-50 mm. The primary outcome was a composite of 30‑day mortality, stroke, or acute kidney injury, with secondary outcomes including long‑term survival and postoperative complications. MATERIAL AND METHODS: n n This single‑center observational cohort included patients treated between 2016 and 2024. Distal ascending aortic diameters were assessed on preoperative computed tomography, and clinical data were obtained from SWEDEHEART. Patients were assigned to aortic cross‑clamp ( = 261) or MHCA ( = 138). Propensity score matching was performed in a 1:1 ratio to balance baseline characteristics. RESULTS: p p The composite primary outcome occurred in 15 patients (3.8%) and was more common with MHCA than with cross‑clamp (6.5% vs 2.3%, = 0.035). Two patients (0.5%), both in the MHCA group, died within 30 days. After matching, the odds ratio for the composite endpoint was 2.4 (95% CI, 0.66-11.5), indicating no significant difference. Long‑term survival was similar between groups (log‑rank = 0.33). CONCLUSIONS: Both strategies were associated with low perioperative risk and comparable long‑term survival. These results support flexible operative planning, allowing the distal anastomotic technique to be chosen based on individual anatomy and surgical preference.

title: Delayed deterioration after surgical treatment of a spinal dural arteriovenous fistula detected by three spinal angiographies: Case report.
abstract: Spinal dural arteriovenous fistulas (DAVFs) are the most common subtype of spinal arteriovenous malformations, and they often cause progressive myelopathy. Early detection and intervention are critical to preventing irreversible neurological deficits. Selective spinal angiography remains the gold standard for diagnosing this condition. However, for some patients with typical clinical features and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings consistent with DAVF, the initial angiography may fail to detect the lesion. In this article, we report a case of T4 low-flow spinal DAVF that was only identified after three rounds of spinal angiography. The fistula was successfully occluded via surgery, and the patient's symptoms gradually improved postoperatively. Nevertheless, the patient later developed recurrent, aggravated symptoms. The delayed deterioration of previously resolved symptoms was attributed to venous thrombosis, and the condition improved after systemic anticoagulation therapy with heparin. The patients fluctuating symptoms stabilized one month after combined therapy with anticoagulants and antiplatelet drugs. For patients with a high clinical suspicion of spinal DAVF, required to confirm the final diagnosis. Delayed deterioration can occur secondary to progressive venous thrombosis, so preventive anticoagulation is indicated for selected patient's, and this intervention should be individualized.

title: Duplex ultrasound as an initial imaging clue to spontaneous isolated celiac artery dissection: A case report.
abstract: Spontaneous isolated celiac artery dissection is uncommon and is usually confirmed with computed tomography angiography (CTA). Duplex ultrasound may provide an initial clue when the lesion and its flow abnormalities are directly visualized. A 56-year-old woman with untreated hypertension presented with acute persistent epigastric pain radiating to the back. Color Doppler ultrasound at the celiac artery origin demonstrated an intimal flap separating the true and false lumens, with an adjacent hypoechoic component without detectable flow. Spectral Doppler sampling within the dissected segment showed a peak systolic velocity of 225 cm/s with spectral broadening. Initial CTA confirmed proximal celiac artery dissection. On short-interval repeat imaging, the maximum outer diameter at the same anatomic level increased from 8.8 mm to 9.7 mm, the true lumen became more compressed, and new false-lumen thrombosis appeared. Symptoms had not progressed; the decision to intervene was driven by imaging progression. False-lumen coil embolization and stent placement were performed. Follow-up CTA demonstrated a patent stent, preserved major branch perfusion, and no residual false-lumen opacification. In this patient, duplex ultrasound provided an initial imaging clue, whereas CTA confirmed the diagnosis, documented interval remodeling, and assessed the post-treatment anatomy.

title: Functional connectivity recovers canine-human network homology along the evolutionary cortical hierarchy.
abstract: ≈ p = 0.002 p > 0.3 p = 0.93 Mapping functional brain organization between species is a prerequisite for translating connectivity biomarkers from animal models to patients, but connectivity-based correspondence has been demonstrated almost exclusively in primates. We tested whether canine-human network homology can be recovered from functional connectivity alone, using only five network-level anatomical priors, and benchmarked a spectral manifold alignment framework (Laplacian-eigenmap embedding with Procrustes alignment on network centroids) against a simple connectivity-signature matching baseline. Data comprised resting-state fMRI from 15 canines with endovascular permanent middle cerebral artery occlusion (pre-occlusion baseline and hyperacute post-occlusion sessions) and two public OpenNeuro datasets: 29 chronic-phase post-stroke aphasia patients scanned before and after rehabilitation (ds003999) and 10 healthy controls (ds000224). Held-out canine-human network homologies were recovered well above chance (top-5 network correspondence up to 54.5% vs. permutation null18%,), and correspondence followed the evolutionary cortical hierarchy: visual and somatomotor homologies were recovered several-fold above chance, default-mode only weakly-extending a gradient previously described in primates to a carnivore. Notably, simple signature matching (54.5%) outperformed manifold alignment (35.5%), indicating that the homology signal is strong enough to be captured without embedding machinery at translational cohort sizes. Within species, canine network metrics showed no treatment-arm differences (all), and chronic-phase patients did not differ from controls in modularity (); a sensitivity analysis bounds these nulls. All results are fully reproducible from shared code and public data.

title: Surgical, endovascular, and systemic management of renal cell carcinoma with intravascular recurrence.
abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) recurrence within the vasculature represents a rare and challenging clinical scenario with limited evidence to guide management. We report a patient with clear cell RCC and level 4 IVC thrombus who underwent successful radical nephrectomy with IVC thrombectomy and subsequently developed disease recurrence in the supradiaphragmatic IVC and pulmonary arteries. Multidisciplinary management included novel endovascular removal of the recurrent IVC tumor followed by pulmonary bilobectomy for progressive tumor emboli. The patient remains without evidence of recurrent disease. This case highlights the complex multidisciplinary decision-making and potential role of minimally invasive endovascular techniques in managing intravascular RCC.

title: A method for expressing two proteins at a tunable ratio allows for studying the kinetics of creatine transport by MCT12.
abstract: M Interactions between physically or functionally coupled proteins are often studied by co-expression from the same or separate plasmids, but protein ratios can vary widely between individual cells. To overcome this limitation, we developed a strategy to generate tunable and constant expression ratios using a single vector encoding two proteins separated by a P2A site followed by short AAA codon repeats that progressively reduce ribosomal readthrough. After validating this approach with the fluorescent proteins eGFP and mCherry, we applied it to characterize the transport cycle of the electroneutral monocarboxylate transporter MCT12, a task that is otherwise difficult to achieve experimentally. By co-expressing MCT12 with the concentrative creatine transporter CRT1 at defined ratios, we were able to determine the substrate turnover rate of MCT12 and its substrate K. This approach enables precise control of protein stoichiometry, facilitating quantitative mechanistic studies of interacting proteins in cells.

title: Combined antegrade and retrograde transarterial approaches for embolization of a traumatic carotid‑cavernous fistula with concomitant middle meningeal arteriovenous fistula.
abstract: Endovascular treatment (EVT) is a useful modality for traumatic carotid‑cavernous fistulas (CCFs); in rare cases, combined antegrade and retrograde transarterial approaches may be applied for embolization of the fistula with concomitant internal carotid artery (ICA) sacrifice and preservation of the ophthalmic artery (OphA). A 62‑year‑old female patient sustained a motor vehicle accident and developed proptosis, chemosis, and congestion in her right eye, while no abnormalities in ocular motility or visual acuity were noted. Computed tomography angiography confirmed the CCF. Under general anesthesia, digital subtraction angiography revealed a right CCF supplied antegradely by the ICA and retrogradely by the posterior communicating artery (PcomA). A left middle meningeal arteriovenous fistula was identified. Access to the basilar artery was established. A microcatheter was retrogradely navigated via the PcomA to reach the proximal ICA across the fistula. Then, another microcatheter was advanced into the cavernous sinus via an antegrade ICA approach. Subsequently, combined antegrade and retrograde transarterial coiling with ICA sacrifice for the CCF was successfully performed. During coiling, the patency of the OphA was monitored through the PcomA microcatheter. Afterwards, the middle meningeal arteriovenous fistula was embolized. At the 1‑month follow‑up, her right eye redness and swelling resolved, and at the 3‑month follow‑up, she had recovered well and returned to her normal status. Therefore, when embolizing the CCF with ICA sacrifice, if the PcomA is well‑developed, the combined antegrade and retrograde transarterial approaches can be used, which may facilitate the obliteration of the CCF and preservation of the OphA.

title: Meta-analysis of the histopathological features of surgically removed aortas classified according to the SCVP and AECVP consensus documents.
abstract: The Society for Cardiovascular Pathology (SCVP) and the Association for European Cardiovascular Pathology (AECVP) published consensus statements on the surgical pathology of the aorta to unify nomenclature and provide a new classification scheme to systematically evaluate the degenerative and inflammatory lesions of the thoracic aorta. The aim of this meta-analysis was to determine the histopathological features of thoracic aneurysmatic aortas, thoracic dissected aortas, and thoracic aortas in patients with a bicuspid aortic valve (BAV). Additionally, the aim was to map how consensus documents and classification schemes is used in practice and research. Articles for analysis were identified while searching for references to the SCVP and AECVP consensus documents, resulting in 174 articles. After applying the exclusion and inclusion criteria, 10 articles were included in the analysis. Four cohorts were analysed: the whole cohort, the aneurysm cohort, the dissection cohort, and the BAV cohort. Medial degeneration was found in all cohorts. The dissection cohort showed more severe medial degeneration than the aneurysm cohort or the BAV cohort. The BAV cohort showed the mildest medial degeneration compared to the other cohorts. More prevalent smooth muscle cell nuclei loss was linked to dissection. The BAV cohort showed milder changes in elastic fibers. Atherosclerosis was comparable among all cohorts. Medial degeneration represents the pathological process of several aortic diseases. All studied components of medial degeneration were present in aneurysms, dissections, and BAV aortas. The consensus documents have been useful tools and assist with the systematic evaluation of resected aortas, although their use in the complexity is limited.

title: Predictors of Successful Integrated Vascular Surgery Residency Match: A Texas Star Database Analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aims to determine factors predictive of successful matching into vascular surgery residency. This has been studied in other fields, but there is a paucity of data specific to vascular surgery. This information can be helpful in guiding medical students interested in applying for this competitive field. METHODS: The Texas Seeking Transparency in Application to Residency database was used to analyze self-reported demographics, match results, and application variables from 2017 to 2025. Multiple characteristics of matched applicants were compared to unmatched applicants. Categorical variables were analyzed using the chi-square test, while continuous variables were assessed with nonparametric tests. Univariate and multivariate logistic regressions were performed to identify predictors of successful matches. RESULTS: A total of 170 applicants responded to the survey, 138 (81%) of whom matched. Those who matched had higher numbers of programs applied to (55 vs 46, p = 0.031), interviews offered (29 vs 20, p = 0.004), interviews attended (21 vs 13, p < 0.001), received an MD vs DO degree (82.5% vs 25%, p = 0.024), and had a vascular rotation at their home institution (85.0% vs 28.6%, p = 0.006). The number of interviews attended was the only significant predictor of matching (OR = 1.96, p = 0.021), with each additional interview attended increasing the odds of matching by 9%. The number of abstracts, posters, and presentations is independently associated with a higher number of interview offers (β = 0.86, p = 0.01), with each additional abstract, publication, or poster associated with an average increase of 0.86 interview invitations. CONCLUSIONS: This study reinforces the idea that going on more interviews increases the chances of matching. Applicants with a higher number of abstracts, posters, or presentations received more interview invites. Geographic signaling, USMLE exam scores, clerkships with honors, and honorary membership in societies were not associated with a higher chance of matching.
